course_name_original: Ethics and academic integrity in computer science
course_name_en: Ethics and academic integrity in computer science

learning_outcomes.text: The graduate has the necessary knowledge to review specialized literature.
The graduate has the ability to observe and obtain information from various sources.
The graduate is able to define/identify/understand research problems in the field of computer science.
The student has the ability to work independently to develop subject-specific assignments.

syllabus_topics: The nature of ethics. Applied ethics and deontological ethics.
Whistle – Blowing between morality and legislation.
Main ethical dilemmas of the digital economy and society (freedom vs determinism).
The main ethical dilemmas of Big Tech.
Ethics of disruptive technologies and innovations.
Ethical dilemmas of data-centric business models.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment: Assimilation and appropriation of information received, reasoning, critical and creative thinking on course topics. Dialogues within the course.
Presentation of the final project: Application of ethical principles and professional deontology in computer science.

assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 5 is required for both evaluation stages (continuous assessment and final project).
